title: Guarded Call Runtime Toggle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Instrumentation
JavaScript
p5.js
Defensive Programming
description: A p5.js demonstration in which learners toggle the xAPI runtime on and off and switch between guarded and unguarded instrumentation calls, observing the highlighted line, the status (Runs or ReferenceError: LRSSim is not defined) and whether a statement is recorded.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The guarded call pattern for instrumented p5.js MicroSims
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish a guarded from an unguarded instrumentation call by observing what each does when the runtime is present and when it is absent.
prerequisites: The LRS runtime script and handles (Chapter 17)
Basic p5.js structure: setup(), draw() and control callbacks

accessibility.notes: Native checkbox, radio buttons and button; status is given in words (Runs, error text) as well as color

controls.label: Runtime loaded (off = the p5.js editor)
controls.purpose: Simulate the runtime files being present or absent

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Contrasting cases with an observation grid
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Toggle two factors, trigger an event, compare highlighted code and outcomes
keyQuestions: Which line throws when the runtime is absent, and why does draw() never start?
Why does the guarded sketch record nothing without the runtime?
Do the two styles differ when the runtime is present?
commonMisconceptions: A missing runtime only disables recording, whatever the code
Guarding the creation line is enough; later uses need no guard
The p5.js editor loads the book's runtime files
assessmentOpportunities: Rewriting an unguarded call as a guarded one

simulation.model: State machine simulating setup() and the slider handler with and without window.LRSSim
assumptions: The runtime is simulated in the sketch; nothing is sent
Full mode is assumed when a statement is recorded
